warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:8: Metformin-associated lactic acidosis was characterized by elevated blood lactate concentrations (> 5mmol/L), anion gap acidosis (without evidence of ketonuria or ketonemia), and an increased lactate: pyruvate ratio; metformin plasma levels were generally > 5 mcg/mL.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:9: Metformin decreases liver uptake of lactate increasing lactate blood levels which may increase the risk of lactic acidosis, especially in patients at risk.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:10: If metformin-associated lactic acidosis is suspected, general supportive measures should be instituted promptly in a hospital setting, along with immediate discontinuation of metformin hydrochloride.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:11: In metformin hydrochloride treated patients with a diagnosis or strong suspicion of lactic acidosis, prompt hemodialysis is recommended to correct the acidosis and remove accumulated metformin (metformin hydrochloride is dialyzable with a clearance of up to 170 mL/min under good hemodynamic conditions).
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:12: Hemodialysis has often resulted in reversal of symptoms and recovery.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:13: Educate patients and their families about the symptoms of lactic acidosis and, if these symptoms occur, instruct them to discontinue metformin hydrochloride and report these symptoms to their healthcare provider.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:14: For each of the known and possible risk factors for metformin-associated lactic acidosis, recommendations to reduce the risk of and manage metformin-associated lactic acidosis are provided below:

warnings_and_cautions:15.lead_in: For each of the known and possible risk factors for metformin-associated lactic acidosis, recommendations to reduce the risk of and manage metformin-associated lactic acidosis are provided below:
warnings_and_cautions:15.text: Renal impairment —The postmarketing metformin-associated lactic acidosis cases primarily occurred in patients with significant renal impairment.

warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:16: The risk of metformin accumulation and metformin-associated lactic acidosis increases with the severity of renal impairment because metformin is substantially excreted by the kidney.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:17: Clinical recommendations based upon the patient’s renal function include [see Dosage and Administration ( 2.3 ), Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 ) ]: o Before initiating metformin hydrochloride, obtain an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). o Metformin hydrochloride is contraindicated in patients with an eGFR less than 30 mL/min/1.73 m 2 [see Contraindications ( 4 ) ]. o Initiation of metformin hydrochloride is not recommended in patients with eGFR between 30 to 45 mL/min/1.73 m 2 . o Obtain an eGFR at least annually in all patients taking metformin hydrochloride.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:18: In patients at risk for the development of renal impairment (e.g., the elderly), renal function should be assessed more frequently. o In patients taking metformin hydrochloride whose eGFR falls below 45 mL/min/1.73 m 2 , assess the benefit and risk of continuing therapy.

warnings_and_cautions:19.lead_in: For each of the known and possible risk factors for metformin-associated lactic acidosis, recommendations to reduce the risk of and manage metformin-associated lactic acidosis are provided below:
warnings_and_cautions:19.text: Drug interactions — The concomitant use of metformin hydrochloride with specific drugs may increase the risk of metformin-associated lactic acidosis: those that impair renal function, result in significant hemodynamic change, interfere with acid-base balance, or increase metformin accumulation.

warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:20: Consider more frequent monitoring of patients [ see Drug Interactions ( 7 ) ].

warnings_and_cautions:21.lead_in: For each of the known and possible risk factors for metformin-associated lactic acidosis, recommendations to reduce the risk of and manage metformin-associated lactic acidosis are provided below:
warnings_and_cautions:21.text: Age 65 or greater — The risk of metformin-associated lactic acidosis increases with the patient’s age because elderly patients have a greater likelihood of having hepatic, renal, or cardiac impairment than younger patients.

warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:22: Assess renal function more frequently in elderly patients.

warnings_and_cautions:23.lead_in: For each of the known and possible risk factors for metformin-associated lactic acidosis, recommendations to reduce the risk of and manage metformin-associated lactic acidosis are provided below:
warnings_and_cautions:23.text: Radiologic studies with contrast —Administration of intravascular iodinated contrast agents in metformin-treated patients has led to an acute decrease in renal function and the occurrence of lactic acidosis.

warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:24: Stop metformin hydrochloride at the time of, or prior to, an iodinated contrast imaging procedure in patients with an eGFR between 30 and 60 mL/min/1.73 m 2 ; in patients with a history of hepatic impairment, alcoholism or heart failure; or in patients who will be administered intra-arterial iodinated contrast.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:25: Re-evaluate eGFR 48 hours after the imaging procedure, and restart metformin hydrochloride if renal function is stable.

warnings_and_cautions:26.lead_in: For each of the known and possible risk factors for metformin-associated lactic acidosis, recommendations to reduce the risk of and manage metformin-associated lactic acidosis are provided below:
warnings_and_cautions:26.text: Surgery and other procedures — Withholding of food and fluids during surgical or other procedures may increase the risk for volume depletion, hypotension, and renal impairment.

warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:27: Metformin hydrochloride should be temporarily discontinued while patients have restricted food and fluid intake.

warnings_and_cautions:28.lead_in: For each of the known and possible risk factors for metformin-associated lactic acidosis, recommendations to reduce the risk of and manage metformin-associated lactic acidosis are provided below:
warnings_and_cautions:28.text: Hypoxic states — Several of the postmarketing cases of metformin-associated lactic acidosis occurred in the setting of acute congestive heart failure (particularly when accompanied by hypoperfusion and hypoxemia).

warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:29: Cardiovascular collapse (shock), acute myocardial infarction, sepsis, and other conditions associated with hypoxemia have been associated with lactic acidosis and may cause prerenal azotemia.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:30: When such an event occurs, discontinue metformin hydrochloride.

warnings_and_cautions:31.lead_in: For each of the known and possible risk factors for metformin-associated lactic acidosis, recommendations to reduce the risk of and manage metformin-associated lactic acidosis are provided below:
warnings_and_cautions:31.text: Excessive alcohol intake — Alcohol potentiates the effect of metformin on lactate metabolism.

warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:32: Patients should be warned against excessive alcohol intake while receiving metformin hydrochloride.

warnings_and_cautions:33.lead_in: For each of the known and possible risk factors for metformin-associated lactic acidosis, recommendations to reduce the risk of and manage metformin-associated lactic acidosis are provided below:
warnings_and_cautions:33.text: Hepatic impairment — Patients with hepatic impairment have developed cases of metformin-associated lactic acidosis.

warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:34: This may be due to impaired lactate clearance resulting in higher lactate blood levels.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:35: Therefore, avoid use of metformin hydrochloride in patients with clinical or laboratory evidence of hepatic disease.

warnings_and_cautions:36.lead_in: For each of the known and possible risk factors for metformin-associated lactic acidosis, recommendations to reduce the risk of and manage metformin-associated lactic acidosis are provided below:
warnings_and_cautions:36.text: Mitochondrial Diseases :Metformin may increase the risk of lactic acidosis in patients with mitochondrial diseases such as mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes (MELAS) syndrome and maternally inherited diabetes and deafness (MIDD).

warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:37: Metformin hydrochloride oral solution is not recommended in patients with mitochondrial diseases such as MELAS syndrome and MIDD.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:38: Ifa patient taking metformin hydrochloride oral solution develops elevated lactic acid levels (with or without accompanying neurologic signs and symptoms), discontinue metformin hydrochloride oral solution.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:39: Depending on the clinical context, consider evaluating the patient for MELAS, MIDD, or other mitochondrial disease. 5.2 Vitamin B 12 Deficiency In clinical trials of 29-week duration with metformin hydrochloride (HCl) tablets, a decrease to subnormal levels of previously normal serum vitamin B 12 levels was observed in approximately 7% of patients.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:40: Such decrease, possibly due to interference with B 12 absorption from the B 12 -intrinsic factor complex, may be associated with anemia but appears to be rapidly reversible with discontinuation of metformin or vitamin B 12 supplementation.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:41: Certain individuals (those with inadequate vitamin B 12 or calcium intake or absorption) appear to be predisposed to developing subnormal vitamin B 12 levels.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:42: Measure hematologic parameters on an annual basis and vitamin B 12 at 2 to 3 year intervals in patients on metformin hydrochloride and manage any abnormalities [see Adverse Reactions ( 6.1 ) ]. 5.3 Hypoglycemia with Concomitant Use with Insulin and Insulin Secretagogues Insulin and insulin secretagogues (e.g., sulfonylurea) are known to cause hypoglycemia.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:43: Metformin hydrochloride may increase the risk of hypoglycemia when combined with insulin and/or an insulin secretagogue.
warnings_and_cautions.warnings_and_cautions:44: Therefore, a lower dose of insulin or insulin secretagogue may be required to minimize the risk of hypoglycemia when used in combination with metformin hydrochloride [see Drug Interactions ( 7 )]. 5.4 Macrovascular Outcomes There have been no clinical studies establishing conclusive evidence of macrovascular risk reduction with metformin hydrochloride.

drug_interactions.drug_interactions:1: 7 DRUG INTERACTIONS Table 2 presents clinically significant drug interactions with metformin hydrochloride.
drug_interactions.drug_interactions:2: Table 2: Clinically Significant Drug Interactions with Metformin Hydrochloride Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibitors Clinical Impact: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors frequently cause a decrease in serum bicarbonate and induce non-anion gap, hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis.
drug_interactions.drug_interactions:3: Concomitant use of these drugs with metformin hydrochloride may increase the risk for lactic acidosis.
drug_interactions.drug_interactions:4: Intervention: Consider more frequent monitoring of these patients.
drug_interactions.drug_interactions:5: Examples: Topiramate, zonisamide, acetazolamide or dichlorphenamide.
drug_interactions.drug_interactions:6: Drugs that Reduce Metformin Hydrochloride Clearance Clinical Impact: Concomitant use of drugs that interfere with common renal tubular transport systems involved in the renal elimination of metformin (e.g., organic cationic transporter-2 [OCT 2 ] / multidrug and toxin extrusion [MATE] inhibitors) could increase systemic exposure to metformin and may increase the risk for lactic acidosis [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )].
drug_interactions.drug_interactions:7: Intervention: Consider the benefits and risks of concomitant use with metformin hydrochloride.
drug_interactions.drug_interactions:8: Examples: Ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, and cimetidine.
drug_interactions.drug_interactions:9: Alcohol Clinical Impact: Alcohol is known to potentiate the effect of metformin on lactate metabolism.
drug_interactions.drug_interactions:10: Intervention: Warn patients against excessive alcohol intake while receiving metformin hydrochloride.
drug_interactions.drug_interactions:11: Insulin Secretagogues or Insulin Clinical Impact: Coadministration of metformin hydrochloride with an insulin secretagogue (e.g., sulfonylurea) or insulin may increase the risk of hypoglycemia.
drug_interactions.drug_interactions:12: Intervention: Patients receiving an insulin secretagogue or insulin may require lower doses of the insulin secretagogue or insulin.
drug_interactions.drug_interactions:13: Drugs Affecting Glycemic Control Clinical Impact: Certain drugs tend to produce hyperglycemia and may lead to loss of glycemic control.
drug_interactions.drug_interactions:14: Intervention: When such drugs are administered to a patient receiving metformin hydrochloride, observe the patient closely for loss of blood glucose control.
drug_interactions.drug_interactions:15: When such drugs are withdrawn from a patient receiving metformin hydrochloride, observe the patient closely for hypoglycemia.
drug_interactions.drug_interactions:16: Examples: Thiazides and other diuretics, corticosteroids, phenothiazines, thyroid products, estrogens, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, nicotinic acid, sympathomimetics, calcium channel blockers, and isoniazid.

drug_interactions:17.lead_in: Examples: Thiazides and other diuretics, corticosteroids, phenothiazines, thyroid products, estrogens, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, nicotinic acid, sympathomimetics, calcium channel blockers, and isoniazid.
drug_interactions:17.text: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors may increase risk of lactic acidosis.

drug_interactions:19.lead_in: Examples: Thiazides and other diuretics, corticosteroids, phenothiazines, thyroid products, estrogens, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, nicotinic acid, sympathomimetics, calcium channel blockers, and isoniazid.
drug_interactions:19.text: Drugs that reduce metformin clearance (such as ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, and cimetidine) may increase the accumulation of metformin.

drug_interactions.drug_interactions:20: Consider the benefits and risks of concomitant use ( 7 )

drug_interactions:21.lead_in: Examples: Thiazides and other diuretics, corticosteroids, phenothiazines, thyroid products, estrogens, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, nicotinic acid, sympathomimetics, calcium channel blockers, and isoniazid.
drug_interactions:21.text: Alcohol can potentiate the effect of metformin on lactate metabolism.

drug_interactions.drug_interactions:22: Warn patients against excessive alcohol intake ( 7 )

information_for_patients.information_for_patients:1: 17 PATIENT COUNSELING INFORMATION Advise the patient to read the FDA-approved patient labeling (Patient Information).
information_for_patients.information_for_patients:2: Administration: Instruct patients or caregivers to use the supplied dosing cup to measure the prescribed amount of medication.
information_for_patients.information_for_patients:3: Inform patients that additional metformin hydrochloride oral solution dosing cups or oral dosing syringes may be obtained from their pharmacy.
information_for_patients.information_for_patients:4: Lactic Acidosis: Explain the risks of lactic acidosis, its symptoms, and conditions that predispose to its development.
information_for_patients.information_for_patients:5: Advise patients to discontinue metformin hydrochloride oral solution immediately and to promptly notify their healthcare provider if unexplained hyperventilation, myalgias, malaise, unusual somnolence or other nonspecific symptoms occur.
information_for_patients.information_for_patients:6: Counsel patients against excessive alcohol intake and inform patients about importance of regular testing of renal function while receiving metformin hydrochloride oral solution.
information_for_patients.information_for_patients:7: Instruct patients to inform their doctor that they are taking metformin hydrochloride oral solution prior to any surgical or radiological procedure, as temporary discontinuation may be required [ see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 ) ].
information_for_patients.information_for_patients:8: Hypoglycemia Inform patients that hypoglycemia may occur when metformin hydrochloride oral solution is coadministered with oral sulfonylureas and insulin.
information_for_patients.information_for_patients:9: Explain to patients receiving concomitant therapy the risks of hypoglycemia, its symptoms and treatment, and conditions that predispose to its development [ see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.3 ) ].
information_for_patients.information_for_patients:10: Vitamin B 12 Deficiency: Inform patients about importance of regular hematological parameters while receiving metformin hydrochloride oral solution [ see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.2 ) ].
information_for_patients.information_for_patients:11: Females of Reproductive Age: Inform females that treatment with metformin hydrochloride oral solution may result in ovulation in some premenopausal anovulatory women which may lead to unintended pregnancy [see Use in Specific Populations ( 8.3 )].
information_for_patients.information_for_patients:12: Manufactured for: Camber Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Piscataway, NJ 08854 By: Annora Pharma Pvt. Ltd. Sangareddy - 502313, Telangana, India.

boxed_warning.boxed_warning:1: WARNING: LACTIC ACIDOSIS Postmarketing cases of metformin-associated lactic acidosis have resulted in death, hypothermia, hypotension, and resistant bradyarrhythmias.
boxed_warning.boxed_warning:2: The onset of metformin-associated lactic acidosis is often subtle, accompanied only by nonspecific symptoms such as malaise, myalgias, respiratory distress, somnolence, and abdominal pain.
boxed_warning.boxed_warning:3: Metformin-associated lactic acidosis was characterized by elevated blood lactate levels (>5 mmol/Liter), anion gap acidosis (without evidence of ketonuria or ketonemia), an increased lactate/pyruvate ratio; and metformin plasma levels generally >5 mcg/mL [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 )].
boxed_warning.boxed_warning:4: Risk factors for metformin-associated lactic acidosis include renal impairment, concomitant use of certain drugs (e.g. carbonic anhydrase inhibitors such as topiramate), age 65 years old or greater, having a radiological study with contrast, surgery and other procedures, hypoxicstates (e.g., acute congestive heart failure), excessive alcohol intake, hepatic impairment and mitochondrial diseases [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1)] .
boxed_warning.boxed_warning:5: Steps to reduce the risk of and manage metformin-associated lactic acidosis in these high risk groups are provided [see Dosage and Administration ( 2.3 ), Contraindications ( 4 ), Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 ) ].
boxed_warning.boxed_warning:6: If metformin-associated lactic acidosis is suspected, immediately discontinue metformin hydrochloride oral solution and institute general supportive measures in a hospital setting.
boxed_warning.boxed_warning:7: Prompt hemodialysis is recommended [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 ) ].
boxed_warning.boxed_warning:8: WARNING: LACTIC ACIDOSIS See full prescribing information for complete boxed warning

boxed_warning:9.lead_in: WARNING: LACTIC ACIDOSIS See full prescribing information for complete boxed warning
boxed_warning:9.text: Postmarketing cases of metformin-associated lactic acidosis have resulted in death, hypothermia, hypotension, and resistant bradyarrhythmias.

boxed_warning.boxed_warning:10: Symptoms included malaise, myalgias, respiratory distress, somnolence, and abdominal pain.
boxed_warning.boxed_warning:11: Laboratory abnormalities included elevated blood lactate levels, anion gap acidosis, increased lactate/pyruvate ratio; and metformin plasma levels generally > 5 mcg/mL. ( 5.1 )

boxed_warning:12.lead_in: WARNING: LACTIC ACIDOSIS See full prescribing information for complete boxed warning
boxed_warning:12.text: Risk factors include renal impairment, concomitant use of certain drugs, age ≥ 65 years old, radiological studies with contrast, surgery and other procedures, hypoxic states, excessive alcohol intake, hepatic impairment and mitochondrial diseases.

boxed_warning.boxed_warning:13: Steps to reduce the risk of and manage metformin-associated lactic acidosis in these high risk groups are provided in the Full Prescribing Information. ( 5.1)

boxed_warning:14.lead_in: WARNING: LACTIC ACIDOSIS See full prescribing information for complete boxed warning
boxed_warning:14.text: If lactic acidosis is suspected, discontinue metformin hydrochloride oral solution and institute general supportive measures in a hospital setting.

sections.active_ingredient: Active ingredient (in each 5 mL teaspoonful) Loratadine 5 mg
sections.indications_and_usage: Uses temporarily relieves these symptoms due to hay fever or other upper respiratory allergies: • runny nose • itchy, watery eyes • sneezing • itching of the nose or throat
sections.warnings: Warnings Do not use if you have ever had an allergic reaction to this product or any of its ingredients Ask a doctor before use if you have liver or kidney disease. Your doctor should determine if you need a different dose. When using this product do not take more than directed. Taking more than directed may cause drowsiness. Stop use and ask a doctor if an allergic reaction to this product occurs. Seek medical help right away. If pregnant or breast feeding, ask a health professional before use. Keep out of reach of children. In case of overdose, get medical help or contact a Poison Control Center right away (1-800-222-1222).
sections.do_not_use: Do not use if you have ever had an allergic reaction to this product or any of its ingredients

sections.stop_use: Stop use and ask a doctor if an allergic reaction to this product occurs. Seek medical help right away.
sections.pregnancy_or_breast_feeding: If pregnant or breast feeding, ask a health professional before use.
sections.keep_out_of_reach_of_children: Keep out of reach of children. In case of overdose, get medical help or contact a Poison Control Center right away (1-800-222-1222).

sections.storage_and_handling: Other information • do not use if carton is opened, or if printed neckband is broken or missing • store between 20° to 25°C (68° to 77°F)
